text:
Sara K: Heads up — we had another 'card flicker' on gw-node-42 in eu-west1, Xid bursts then transient pci errors. Not a clean ECC pattern.
Vik P: Saw that alert. infra-bot reported 5 xid events in ~30s then resolved. Node stayed healthy from kubernetes perspective.
Marta L: Is this the same as last week's flapper? Last time drain automation cordoned 6 nodes in the same window and we hit capacity shortage.
Devon: Yep similar symptoms but shorter burst. We should avoid aggressive auto-drain for these short pulses. Suggest adding a rate limiter and hysteresis to the autodrain rules.
Sara K: Agreed. Current rule: if xid_count >= 3 within 60s -> cordon + evict. That triggers too easily for transient PCI resets.
Marta L: Proposal: require either (a) repeated bursts in multiple 5min windows OR (b) xid + temp spike OR (c) post-burst memtest fail. Also add global cooldown per-zone to avoid cascading drains.
Vik P: +1. Also need different behavior for Dedicated vs On-demand pools — can't evict Reserved capacity willy-nilly.
infra-bot: [alert] node gw-node-42: xid_burst=5 window=30s temp=68C memory_err=0
Devon: Example heuristic I sketched:

- immediate_soft_taint if xid_burst >=4 in 20s (no eviction)
- monitor 15m for recurrence
- hard_cordon+evict only if 2 soft_taints in 15m OR mem errors detected
- zone_cooldown: once 1 hard_cordon happened, suppress new hard cordons in same zone for 10m unless >10% nodes affected

That should keep short flickers from triggering mass evacs.
Sara K: We also need to update our slurm integration: soft_taint should translate to setting GRES scheduling weight to 0.5 instead of draining jobs silently. Currently we have only binary drain path.
Marta L: Good call. For k8s add annotation so scheduler deprioritizes pods rather than immediate eviction. We can let long-running pods migrate on natural churn.
Vik P: Cost angle: every hard cordon that triggers requeue for large batch jobs kills throughput. Last month that costed ~120 GPU-hours of wasted scheduling. Add a metric to track 'auto-drain induced requeue_hours' and alert if monthly > threshold.
Devon: On detection side, can we enrich signals? Combine ECC counters, Xid type (63 vs 45), pci-reset meta, and nvml_watchdog events. Some cards show pci flaps without ECC so our rule should weight signals.
Sara K: Let's add a scoring model: weight(xid_burst)=3, weight(ecc)=5, weight(temp>85)=4, weight(pci_reset)=2. If score >=6 -> soft_taint, >=10 -> hard_cordon. Keep weights as config in configmap.
Marta L: Do we want to auto-create bug tickets for models that cross a threshold? Could push to hardware team with node diagnostics attached.
Vik P: Yes — infra-bot should create a ticket with attached nvml dumps and last 100 syslog lines when a node transitions to hard_cordon.
infra-bot: noted: will attach logs if hard_cordon triggered and include device index + pci slot info
Devon: Edge case: region constraints. In ap-southeast we have tight capacity, so set stricter threshold (higher score needed) to avoid impacting customers. Make threshold per-region override.
Sara K: Also protect Dedicated pools: require manual approval for hard cordon unless diagnostic confidence high. We can still mark a device degraded for scheduling but not evict.
Marta L: Implementation plan:
1) change detector to emit event types (soft_taint, hard_cordon_candidate)
2) controller applies per-region + per-pool policy
3) infra-bot tickets on hard cordon
4) update slurm/gres weight and k8s scheduler hints
5) add metrics: detected_soft, detected_hard, requeue_hours, tickets_created

Vik P: Timeline? Can we get a POC in staging next week?
Devon: I can push a draft PR today with the scoring config + cooldown logic. Need one reviewer for k8s scheduler hints and one for slurm hooks.
Sara K: I'll own rollout plan and runbook changes. Add a 'manual revert' command in the controller UI so oncall can uncordon quickly if it's a false positive.
Marta L: Don't forget to test with synthetic xid bursts generator in staging to validate cooldown and zone limits. I can write harness.
Vik P: Also simulate heavy N autovacuums so we ensure cooldown doesn't suppress needed mass-drain when real widespread failure occurs.
infra-bot: reminder: scheduled maintenance in eu-west1 tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC (non-disruptive)
Devon: Ok I'll open PR draft and tag @Vik P, @Marta L for review.
Sara K: Thanks team. Let's reconvene after PR review and synthetic test. :thumbsup:
